title: Fortran
subtitle: The first high-level language, still at the heart of weather forecasting, climate models and physics codes, taught as modern Fortran 2018 with whole-array operations, modules and objects.
description: Fortran (originally FORTRAN, for *Formula Translation*) was created at IBM by a team led by John Backus, and its first compiler shipped in 1957. It was the first widely used high-level programming language, and it proved that a compiler could produce code nearly as fast as hand-written assembly. Nearly seventy years later it is still a living language, revised by an ISO committee (most recently as Fortran 2023), and it still runs much of the world's heaviest numerical computing: weather and climate models, computational fluid dynamics, quantum chemistry, nuclear and astrophysics codes, and the linear-algebra libraries that Python, R, Julia and MATLAB call under the hood.

This course teaches **modern Fortran**, the free-form language of the 2008 and 2018 standards, not the punched-card FORTRAN 77 many people imagine. It covers the compiler and program structure, types and declarations, control flow, arrays as first-class values, procedures and modules, derived types and object-oriented features, numerical precision, formatted and file I/O, parallelism with `do concurrent`, coarrays, OpenMP and MPI, calling Fortran from C and Python, and the modern tooling of the Fortran-lang community, ending with an orbital-simulation project. It assumes the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience: you know what a variable, a loop and a function are. No previous Fortran is needed.

To run the programs, install **GFortran**, the Fortran compiler of the GNU Compiler Collection (on Debian and Ubuntu `sudo apt install gfortran`, on macOS through Homebrew with `brew install gcc`, on Windows through MSYS2 or WSL); [fortran-lang.org](https://fortran-lang.org/) lists it alongside the other free and commercial compilers, such as LLVM Flang and Intel's ifx. You can also try small programs in the browser in the Fortran-lang community's online playground. Every program marked as checked was compiled by Lumenary's test suite with GFortran 11 using `gfortran -std=f2018 -Wall` and run, and the output shown is the output it printed. The lessons were drafted with AI assistance and are awaiting review by a human computer scientist.

levels.title: The core language
levels.summary: Where Fortran came from and why it endures, compiling a first program, types, declarations and control flow, and the arrays that are Fortran's greatest strength.

levels.title: Building numerical software
levels.summary: Procedures and modules for organising code, kind parameters and floating-point precision, formatted and file input and output, and derived types with Fortran's object-oriented features.

levels.title: Fortran in research and industry
levels.summary: Parallel Fortran with do concurrent, coarrays, OpenMP and MPI, calling Fortran from C and Python, and the fpm package manager and community tools, brought together in an orbital-simulation project.
